title: Form Follows Function: Bridging Neuroscience and Architecture

findings.antecedent: Knowing one's location in a virtual environment
findings.mechanism: Brain areas involved in navigation and visual orientation
findings.quote: Event-related spectral perturbations brainwaves... reveal differences in brain dynamics when subjects know their location compared with EEG components when they are lost.

findings.antecedent: Spaces rich with visual cues in a virtual environment
findings.consequent: EEG responses in parietal and occipitotemporal cortex
findings.mechanism: Brain areas involved in navigation and visual orientation
findings.quote: Differences in EEG responses associated with spaces rich with visual cues versus ambiguous spaces devoid of cues were found in parietal and occipitotemporal cortex.

findings.antecedent: Navigating in virtual environments (implied comparison between conditions leading to EEG differences, e.g., with/without cues)
findings.mechanism: Involvement of brain parts for navigation and visual orientation
findings.quote: A significantly stronger synchronization in theta waves and stronger desynchronization in the lower alpha band of EEG frequencies was observed.

findings.antecedent: Navigating in virtual environments (implied comparison between conditions leading to EEG differences, e.g., with/without cues)
findings.mechanism: Involvement of brain parts for navigation and visual orientation
findings.quote: A significantly stronger synchronization in theta waves and stronger desynchronization in the lower alpha band of EEG frequencies was observed.

findings.antecedent: Disorientation in virtual spaces with less visuospatial information
findings.quote: Disorientation in spaces with less visuospatial information was associated with increased alpha wave desynchronization, likely reflecting increased attentional demands [20].

findings.consequent: Subjects' use of visual cues for navigation
findings.mechanism: Humans seek distinguishing features for wayfinding
findings.quote: These early results indicated a progressively subtle use of visual cues as subjects navigated the ambiguous space.

findings.antecedent: Virtual space without obvious wayfinding cues
findings.consequent: Subjects' search behavior for distinguishing features (e.g., shadows, patterned finishes)
findings.mechanism: Humans seek distinguishing features for wayfinding
findings.quote: In the case where obvious cue were not presented, subjects looked for any distinguishing features that might indicate location, including shadows around doors, or patterned finishes.

findings.antecedent: Brief exposure (less than 15m) to red, bright white, and dark light conditions during memory task performance
findings.quote: heart rate variability... was highly significantly different during memory task performance during brief exposure (less than 15 m) to red, bright white, and dark conditions.

findings.consequent: Cardiac responses (HRV relaxation during rest and activation during memory task)
findings.quote: red light regulated cardiac responses, with appropriate HRV relaxation during rest and activation during the memory task.

findings.antecedent: Bright white light with a blue peak
findings.quote: bright white light with a blue peak was associated with constant heart rate activation throughout the experiment [28].

findings.antecedent: Red light conditions vs. bright white light conditions
findings.quote: brainwaves recorded via a 256 electrode EEG array tended to be different during red versus bright white light conditions in a single subject self-control study [29].

stimuli.description: Immersive 3D virtual reality CAVE displaying full-scale building models and virtual reality simulations of building scenarios

Virtual sound simulation environment (SoniCAVEM) with ultrahigh definition recordings and sound simulations of real environments, including realistic clinical sounds, equipment alarms, and mechanical sounds
Red, bright white (with blue peak), and dark light conditions
Virtual spaces rich with visual cues vs. ambiguous spaces devoid of cues for wayfinding

limitations: Scarcity of research into diagnostic accuracy during masking from ambient HVAC, clinical or equipment sounds within architectural settings.
The influence of “full spectrum” electrical lighting, which has a limited number of spectral peaks within the range of visible light, has yet to be established.

Current sustainable guidelines crediting proportion of space with daylight, rather than adjustable lighting systems for individual needs, are unlikely to address the range of human conditions and dynamically changing functions in architectural settings.
